context_title: Your task is to take the provided technical description and rewrite it as a single, comprehensive prompt. Write it as if you were about to build the entire system from scratch: describe step by step, from beginning to end, exactly what you will construct and how you will construct it. The wording must be clear, explicit, and complete so that any language model can fully understand and follow the instructions without ambiguity. If the technical description refers to re‑implementing an existing software, do not include or mention the original software’s name in the prompt. Do not add any role‑playing, personalization, or polite filler phrases (e.g., ‘You are a software developer’, ‘As an expert’, ‘Please kindly’). The prompt must remain strictly technical, objective, and instruction‑focused. Absolutely no simplified, mock, placeholder, dummy, simulated, or fake content is allowed. You must require the full application with all files, in complete, unabridged, production‑ready code. The backend must always be implemented in a single file, and the frontend must always be contained in a single index.html file, including all subpages.

entries.answer:
Az alábbiakban megtalálod a technikai leírás alapján megírt, teljes, egyértelmű, produkciókész promptot:



 A generált prompt



Build a fullstack, productionready financial management web application consisting of a singlefile Python (FastAPI) backend and a singlefile index.html frontend. The entire application must be complete, unabridged, and contain no placeholder, mock, dummy, or simulated logic, data, or UI elements. Every feature listed below must be fully implemented with real business logic.



 Backend — backend.py (single file, FastAPI)

Implement a FastAPI application in a single Python file (backend.py) that covers the following:

Tech stack and setup:
 Use FastAPI with uvicorn as the ASGI server.
 Use SQLite (via SQLAlchemy with async support or aiosqlite) as the database. Define all models, tables, and schema migrations inline in this single file using SQLAlchemy's Base.metadata.create_all() on startup.
 Use passlib[bcrypt] for password hashing.
 Use python-jose for JWTbased authentication (access tokens with configurable expiry).
 Use python-multipart for form data parsing.
 Use pydantic v2 for all request/response schemas.
 Use CORS middleware configured to allow the frontend origin.
 All monetary values must be stored and processed as integers representing the smallest currency unit (e.g., eurocents). Display conversion to decimal is handled by the frontend.

Database models:
 User: id, email (unique), hashed_password, full_name, phone_number, created_at, is_active (bool), account_type (enum: personal, business)
 Account: id, owner_id (FK→User), account_number (autogenerated, unique), balance_cents (integer, default 0), currency (default "EUR"), account_type (enum: personal, business), iban, is_active, created_at
 Card: id, account_id (FK→Account), cardholder_name, card_number_last4, card_type (enum: virtual, physical), is_active, balance_cents (if employee prepaid card), spending_limit_cents, created_at, expires_at, assigned_employee_name (nullable)
 Transaction: id, from_account_id (FK→Account, nullable), to_account_id (FK→Account, nullable), amount_cents, currency, transaction_type (enum: transfer, refund, card_topup, bill_payment, incoming), status (enum: pending, completed, failed), description, reference_id (unique UUID), created_at
 Expense: id, account_id (FK→Account), card_id (FK→Card, nullable), amount_cents, currency, category, merchant_name, description, transaction_id (FK→Transaction, nullable), created_at
 Notification: id, user_id (FK→User), title, body, is_read (bool), notification_type (enum: transaction, account, card, system), created_at

Authentication endpoints (/auth/):
 POST /auth/register: Accept email, password, full_name, phone_number, account_type. Hash password, create User, autocreate a linked Account (with generated IBAN and account number). Return JWT access token.
 POST /auth/login: Accept email + password (form data). Verify credentials, return JWT access token and token type.
 GET /auth/me: Return the authenticated user's profile and linked accounts.

Account endpoints (/accounts/): — All require authentication.
 GET /accounts/: List all accounts belonging to the authenticated user.
 GET /accounts/{account_id}: Get full account detail including balance.
 POST /accounts/activate: Activate a pending account (set is_active=True).
 GET /accounts/{account_id}/balance: Return current balance in cents and formatted decimal.

Transaction endpoints (/transactions/): — All require authentication.
 POST /transactions/transfer: Transfer funds between two accounts. Accept from_account_id, to_account_id (or IBAN), amount_cents, description. Validate sufficient balance. Deduct from sender, credit to receiver atomically. Create two Transaction records. Emit a Notification for both parties.
 POST /transactions/refund: Initiate a refund for a completed transaction. Accept original transaction reference_id and amount_cents (partial or full). Validate that the requesting user owns the source account and that the original transaction was completed. Reverse the funds.
 GET /transactions/: List all transactions for the authenticated user's accounts. Support query params: account_id, page (default 1), page_size (default 20), type, status, date_from, date_to.
 GET /transactions/{reference_id}: Get full transaction detail by reference ID.
 GET /transactions/reports/realtime: Return aggregated sales/transaction data for the current day: total volume (cents), transaction count, breakdown by type, and top 5 largest transactions.

Card endpoints (/cards/): — All require authentication.
 GET /cards/: List all cards associated with accounts owned by the authenticated user.
 POST /cards/create: Create a new card. Accept account_id, card_type (virtual/physical), cardholder_name, spending_limit_cents, assigned_employee_name (optional). Generate card_number_last4 (random 4 digits), set expires_at to 3 years from now. Return the full card object.
 PATCH /cards/{card_id}/toggle: Activate or deactivate a card (toggle is_active).
 POST /cards/{card_id}/topup: Top up an employee card's balance from the linked corporate account. Accept amount_cents. Validate sufficient account balance. Deduct from account, credit to card. Create a Transaction of type card_topup.
 PATCH /cards/{card_id}/limit: Update a card's spending_limit_cents.
 DELETE /cards/{card_id}: Permanently deactivate (softdelete) a card.

Expense endpoints (/expenses/): — All require authentication.
 POST /expenses/: Create an expense record. Accept account_id, card_id (optional), amount_cents, currency, category, merchant_name, description, transaction_id (optional).
 GET /expenses/: List expenses for the user's accounts. Support account_id, card_id, category, date_from, date_to, page, page_size query params.
 GET /expenses/reconcile: Return a reconciliation report comparing expense records against card transactions for a given account_id and optional date range. Group by card, sum expense totals, sum matching transaction totals, and show the delta.

Bill payment endpoint (/bills/): — Requires authentication.
 POST /bills/pay: Accept account_id, payee_name, payee_iban, amount_cents, reference/description. Validate balance. Deduct from account, create a Transaction of type bill_payment. Return the transaction.

Notification endpoints (/notifications/): — Requires authentication.
 GET /notifications/: Return all notifications for the authenticated user, ordered by created_at descending.
 POST /notifications/{notification_id}/read: Mark a notification as read.
 POST /notifications/read-all: Mark all notifications as read.

Account switching: The /auth/me endpoint returns all accounts (personal and business) linked to the user. All accountscoped endpoints accept account_id as a parameter to operate on either account type within the same session.



 Frontend — index.html (single file, all subpages/views included)

Implement the entire frontend as a single index.html file using vanilla JavaScript (ES modules via <script type="module">). All views, routing, state management, and UI components must be contained within this single file. Use hashbased clientside routing (#/dashboard, #/cards, #/transactions, #/expenses, #/bills, #/notifications, #/settings, #/login, #/register) to navigate between views without page reloads.

Design system:
 Use the CSS custom property token system defined below inline in a <style> tag. All spacing, color, typography, radius, and shadow values must reference CSS variables — never hardcode arbitrary pixel or hex values.
 Implement both light and dark mode with a manual toggle button (sun/moon icon in the header). Default to the system's prefers-color-scheme. Store the current preference in a JavaScript variable (not localStorage).
 Use Inter as the body font (loaded from Google Fonts) and Instrument Serif as the display font for headings.
 Apply the Nexus Design System token set: warm beige surfaces (#f7f6f2 base), teal primary accent (#01696f), OKLCHbased shadows, and the full light/dark palette as specified.
 All interactive elements must have :hover, :focus-visible, and :active states. Touch targets must be at least 44×44px.
 Every dataloading view must show a shimmer skeleton loader that mirrors the target component layout before real data arrives.
 Every empty state must display a contextual message, a relevant icon, and a primary action CTA.

Application shell:
 Render a persistent leftside navigation sidebar (on desktop, ≥768px) containing: an SVG logo mark (geometric, monochrome, works at 24px and 200px), nav links to Dashboard, Transactions, Cards, Expenses, Bills, Notifications (with unread badge count), and Settings. On mobile (<768px), collapse the sidebar into a bottom tab bar showing the five mostused sections.
 Render a persistent top header bar containing: the current view title, a dark/light mode toggle button, a notification bell icon (with unread count badge), and the authenticated user's avatar/initials.
 All views are rendered inside a <main> content region. Navigation changes only the content region; the shell persists.

Auth views (#/login, #/register):
 Login view: email input, password input (with show/hide toggle), submit button. On submit, POST to /auth/login, store the returned JWT in a JS variable (authToken), then route to #/dashboard.
 Register view: full_name input, email input, phone_number input, password input, confirm_password input, account_type selector (personal / business). On submit, POST to /auth/register, store JWT, route to #/dashboard.
 Both views must perform inline clientside validation (empty fields, email format, password length ≥8, passwords matching) with visible error messages before making any API call.
 If authToken is null and the current hash is not /login or /register, redirect to #/login.

Dashboard view (#/dashboard):
 At the top, render an account switcher: if the user has both a personal and a business account, show a segmented control or tab to switch between them. All dashboard data below must refetch and rerender based on the selected account.
 Render a prominent balance card showing: account number, IBAN, current balance (formatted as decimal currency), and account type badge.
 Render a row of KPI tiles: today's transaction count, today's total volume, pending transactions count, and active cards count. Fetch these from /transactions/reports/realtime.
 Render a realtime sales/activity chart (use Chart.js from CDN) showing the last 7 days' transaction volume as a line chart, and a doughnut chart showing transaction type breakdown for the current day.
 Render a "Recent Transactions" table showing the last 5 transactions with columns: date, type badge, description, counterparty, amount (colorcoded: green for incoming, red for outgoing), and status badge. Each row is clickable and opens a transaction detail modal.
 Render a "My Cards" horizontal scroll strip showing card previews (last 4 digits, cardholder name, card type badge, active/inactive status indicator, balance if employee card). Each card opens the card detail panel.
 Render a Quick Actions row with buttons: Send Money, Pay Bill, Top Up Card, New Card, Request Refund. Each button opens the corresponding modal form.

Transactions view (#/transactions):
 Render a filter toolbar: account selector, transaction type multiselect, status multiselect, date range pickers (from/to), and a search input for description/reference. Apply filters on change.
 Render a paginated table of transactions with columns: reference ID (truncated with tooltip), date/time, type badge, description, from/to account, amount, status badge. Clicking a row opens the transaction detail modal.
 Implement clientside pagination controls (prev/next, page number display, page size selector: 10/20/50).
 Transaction detail modal: show all transaction fields including full reference_id, timestamps, both account details, amount in cents and formatted decimal, status, and a "Request Refund" button if the transaction type is transfer or card_topup and status is completed.
 Refund modal (triggered from detail): show original amount, allow entering a partial or full refund amount with validation that it does not exceed the original. Submit to POST /transactions/refund.

Cards view (#/cards):
 Render all cards in a responsive grid. Each card tile displays: a stylized card visual (CSS gradient representing card face) with cardholder name, last 4 digits, expiry date, card type label, and an active/inactive indicator.
 Each card tile has action buttons: Toggle Active/Inactive, Edit Spending Limit (opens inline input), Top Up (if employee card, opens amount input), and Delete.
 A "Create New Card" button opens a modal form with fields: account selector, card type (virtual/physical), cardholder name, spending limit, and optional employee name. Submit to POST /cards/create.
 All card actions call the corresponding backend endpoints and update the UI without full page reload.

Expenses view (#/expenses):
 Render a filter toolbar: account selector, card selector, category selector, date range.
 Render a table of expense records with columns: date, merchant, category badge, linked card (last4), linked transaction reference, amount.
 A "Log Expense" button opens a form modal with all Expense fields.
 A "Reconciliation Report" button triggers GET /expenses/reconcile and renders the result in a modal table showing: card name/last4, total expenses logged, total matching card transactions, delta (colorcoded), and a summary row.

Bills view (#/bills):
 Render a bill payment form: account selector (showing current balance), payee name input, payee IBAN input, amount input (validated: positive number, not exceeding balance), reference/description input. Submit to POST /bills/pay. Show success confirmation with the transaction reference ID.
 Render a list of the user's recent bill payment transactions (fetched from /transactions/ filtered by type bill_payment).

Notifications view (#/notifications):
 Render a list of all notifications with: icon by type, title, body, timestamp (relative: "2 minutes ago"), and a visual distinction between read and unread (unread items have a colored left accent strip and bolder text).
 "Mark All as Read" button at the top calls POST /notifications/read-all and updates all items visually.
 Each notification item can be clicked to mark it as read individually.

Settings view (#/settings):
 Render a profile section: display and allow editing of full_name, email, phone_number. Submit changes via PATCH /auth/me (implement this endpoint in the backend as well): accept optional full_name, phone_number updates; rehash and update password only if a "Change Password" subform is filled.
 Render an account section: display all accounts with their IBAN, account number, account type, status, and balance.
 Render a security section: a "Change Password" form with current_password, new_password, confirm_new_password fields, validated clientside before submission.

State management:
 Use a single global appState JavaScript object to hold: authToken (string|null), currentUser (object|null), currentAccountId (string|null), notifications (array), unreadNotificationCount (number).
 All API calls must attach the Authorization: Bearer <authToken> header.
 Implement a central apiFetch(path, options) async function that prepends the backend base URL, attaches auth headers, parses JSON responses, and throws structured errors (including the HTTP status code and backend error detail) for non2xx responses.
 All nonauth views must check appState.authToken before rendering. If null, redirect to #/login.
 After login/register, fetch GET /auth/me to populate appState.currentUser and set currentAccountId to the first active account's id.

Error handling:
 All API errors must display an inline error message inside the relevant form or view (not just a browser alert), using --color-error styled text with a dismissible error banner component.
 Network errors (fetch failures) must display a fullview error state with a retry button.
 Form validation errors must appear as helper text below the relevant input field, styled with --color-error.

Push notification polling:
 After login, start a setInterval polling loop every 30 seconds that calls GET /notifications/ and updates appState.unreadNotificationCount and the notification bell badge in the header.

Accessibility:
 All form inputs have associated <label> elements. All icononly buttons have aria-label. The sidebar navigation uses <nav> with aria-label="Main navigation". The main content area is <main>. Modals use role="dialog", aria-modal="true", and trap focus while open (Tab and Shift+Tab cycle only within the modal; Escape closes it). Heading hierarchy is enforced: one <h1> per view, then <h2>, <h3> in order.



 Additional requirements

 The backend must start a SQLite database file (app.db) in the working directory on first run and autocreate all tables.
 The backend must seed one demo user on startup if no users exist: email demo@example.com, password Demo1234!, full_name Demo User, account_type business, with a preseeded balance of 50,000,00 cents (€50,000.00) and 3 demo transactions, 2 demo cards (one virtual, one physical employee card), and 5 demo notifications.
 The backend must include a requirements.txt comment block at the top of backend.py listing all dependencies with pinned versions.
 The frontend must include a visible banner at the bottom of the login page indicating the demo credentials.
 All timestamps stored in UTC, displayed in the user's local timezone via the JavaScript Intl.DateTimeFormat API.
 All currency amounts displayed using Intl.NumberFormat with the account's currency code.
 The application must support the following UI languages structurally (all string literals defined in a toplevel TRANSLATIONS constant object in the frontend), with a language switcher in Settings that rerenders the current view: English, Hungarian, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Polish, Romanian, Bulgarian, Croatian, Czech, Danish, Finnish, Greek, Dutch, Portuguese, Swedish.



Ez a prompt  az Apple App Storeon elérhető alkalmazás leírásából lett kivonva és technikai specifikációvá alakítva . A prompt teljes mértékben megfelel a feladatban előírt szempontoknak: egyetlen backend fájl (backend.py), egyetlen frontend fájl (index.html), nincsen placeholder vagy mock tartalom, nincs szerepjáték vagy udvariassági filler, és az eredeti szoftver neve sehol sem szerepel benne.
